title: Steer a drifting parcel back into the centre lane before the scanner arch
instruction: The parcel on the conveyor is drifting toward the open edge. Get it between the two white lines before it reaches the arch, without letting it fall off.
context: Skewed-roller conveyor sections drive parcels sideways to line them up against a side rail; where that rail is missing or ends early, parcels drift off the open side, or reach scanners, label applicators and narrowing guides off-centre and jam them or are misread. Attendants steer each one back into the lane by hand while the line keeps running, allowing for the drift that continues after they let go. Done by: conveyor attendants, parcel sorters and warehouse workers.
setup: The two arm bases stand 61 cm apart on an oak table. A powered roller conveyor (bed 26 cm wide, 74 cm long, rollers' top 4.2 cm above the table, rubber-lagged steel rollers 2.5 cm wide at 3.5 cm pitch) lies across the table, parallel to the line through the arm bases, from 20 to 46 cm in front of it, running from 20 cm toward the right arm to 54 cm toward the left arm from the midpoint between the bases. Its rollers are skewed 15 degrees from square, so their surface (6 cm/s) drives a parcel toward the right arm at 5.8 cm/s and toward the arms at 1.6 cm/s. Its near side (toward the arms) is open, a 4.2 cm drop to the table; along its far side, from the arch to its left end, a grey steel rail (1 cm wide, 54 cm long) stands on the table 3 mm from the rollers, its top 3 cm above theirs. Two white lines (6 mm wide) are painted around the rollers 14 cm apart, centred 33 cm in front of the bases, running from the conveyor's left end to the arch, so they read as two lines along it. A dark steel scanner arch (15 cm long along the conveyor) spans the conveyor from the midpoint between the bases to 15 cm toward the right arm: two legs on the table beside the conveyor, a roof 13 cm above the rollers (its top 14 cm), two inner guides hanging from the roof to 3 mm above the rollers that leave a 20 cm opening centred on the lane (23 to 43 cm in front of the bases), and an end stop across the opening at its far end. A brown cardboard parcel (10 x 10 x 6 cm, 150 g, closed and empty) stands flat on the rollers, square to the conveyor, its centre 29 cm in front of the bases (4 cm toward the open side from the lane's centre) and 44 cm toward the left arm from their midpoint. The conveyor starts as the trial starts (full speed within 0.5 s). Untouched, the parcel drifts off the open side about 6 s later, 10 cm before the arch.
scoring: The parcel crosses when its centre passes the arch's upstream face. 1.0 if it crosses standing upright on the rollers (top face within 15 degrees of vertical, underside within 1 cm of the rollers' top) with its centre within 2 cm of the lane's centre (wholly between the white lines); 0.5 if it crosses so 2 to 5 cm off the centre; 0.25 if it crosses more than 5 cm off. If it never crosses riding on the rollers (held back, jammed against a guide, or lifted past the arch): 0.25 if it stands upright on the rollers when the trial ends, else 0. 0 if it fell off the conveyor (its centre past an edge, or its underside 1.5 cm below the rollers' top) before crossing. What happens after the crossing doesn't change the score.
reset_notes: Stop the conveyor, put the parcel back at its start square to the conveyor, and start the conveyor as the trial starts. Check the parcel isn't crushed.
fidelity: The roller bed is modelled as one flat surface moving at the rollers' surface speed in their skewed drive direction, with isotropic friction (rollers 0.8 / 0.7, cardboard 0.5 / 0.4), without the gaps and small bumps between rollers. The rollers are drawn on it; on a real conveyor they turn in place, so they look still as here. The parcel is a rigid box. The arch's guides hang 3 mm above the rollers.
